name: Tettigoniidae

children.name: Austrosaginae
children.desc: Austrosaginae, the sluggish katydids, are a subfamily of Australian insects within the family Tettigoniidae.

children.name: Bradyporinae
Ephippigerini
children.desc: The Ephippigerini are a tribe of bush crickets in the subfamily Bradyporinae, erected by Brunner von Wattenwyl in 1878.
The Bradyporinae are a subfamily in the family Tettigoniidae (bush crickets or katydids), based on the type genus Bradyporus.

children.name: Conocephalinae
Agraeciini
children.desc: Agraeciini is a large tribe of bush crickets or katydids in the conehead subfamily, Conocephalinae.

children.name: Copiphorini
children.desc: The Copiphorini are a tribe of bush crickets or katydids in the family Tettigoniidae.
Conocephalinae, meaning "conical head", is an Orthopteran subfamily in the family Tettigoniidae.

children.name: Hetrodinae
children.desc: The Hetrodinae are a subfamily of robust bush crickets, also known as armoured katydids, corn crickets, etc.

children.name: Hexacentrinae
children.desc: The Hexacentrinae, are a subfamily of predatory bush crickets or katydids.

children.name: Lipotactinae
children.desc: The Lipotactinae is a small subfamily of Asian bush crickets or katydids; it was originally included with the "Meconematidae".

children.name: Listroscelidinae
children.desc: The Listroscelidinae are a subfamily of the Tettigoniidae found in the Americas, Madagascar, and Australia.

children.name: Meconematinae
children.desc: Meconematinae is a subfamily of the bush crickets, with a worldwide distribution (but very limited representation in Antarctica and North America).

children.name: Mecopodinae
Rentziella
children.auth: Morris, Ingrisch, Willemse, Willemse, De Luca & Klimas, 2025

children.desc: Mecopodinae are a subfamily of bush crickets found in western South America, sub-Saharan Africa, and Asia.

children.name: Phaneropterinae
children.desc: The Phaneropterinae, the sickle-bearing bush crickets or leaf katydids, are a subfamily of insects within the family Tettigoniidae.

children.name: Phyllophorinae
children.desc: The Phyllophorinae is a subfamily of the bush crickets or katydids, found in east Malesia to Australia (with a record from Sri Lanka).

children.name: Pseudophyllinae
Pterophyllini
children.desc: Pterophyllini is a tribe of true katydids in the family Tettigoniidae from the Americas.
The subfamily Pseudophyllinae contains numerous species in the family Tettigoniidae, the katydids or bush crickets.

children.name: Pseudotettigoniinae
children.desc: The Pseudotettigoniinae are an extinct subfamily of the Tettigoniidae.

children.name: Metallacantha
children.auth: Ghirotto, Engelking, Fianco, Sobral, Silva-Neto & Mendes, 2025

children.name: Saginae
children.desc: The Saginae, commonly known as the predatory katydids or predatory bush-crickets, is a subfamily of the family Tettigoniidae (the bush-crickets or katydids).

children.name: Tettigoniinae

img.author: Richard Bartz, Munich aka Makro Freak

children.desc: The Tettigoniinae are a subfamily of bush crickets or katydids, which contains hundreds of species in about twelve tribes.

children.name: Tympanophorinae
children.desc: The Tympanophorinae are a monogeneric subfamily of bush-crickets, sometimes called balloon-winged bush-crickets, erected (as family Tympanophoridae) by Carl Brunner von Wattenwyl in 1893.

children.name: Zaprochilinae
children.desc: Zaprochilinae is a subfamily of bush-crickets found in Australia; the type genus is Zaprochilus.

desc: Insects in the family Tettigoniidae are commonly called katydids (especially in North America) or bush crickets.
